headline: Learned models for peptide sequencing, molecule generation, and MD surrogacy
label: Learned Models For Biomolecular Prediction
summary: Recent preprints and publications pair generative and neural-ODE architectures with mass, pharmacokinetic, and MD-trajectory targets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned components embedded inside domain-structured generative and dynamical frameworks. DiffuNovo enforces precursor mass consistency through a training loss and latent-space control, while Uni-PK places molecular representations inside a neural ODE pharmacokinetic structure to model concentration-time profiles. VFMol couples a per-molecule VAE posterior with discrete flow matching for molecular graph generation and adds KAN-based classifier-free property guidance. BiLSTMK-MD surrogates MD and free-energy perturbation trajectories to reduce sampling requirements. The exact-simulation preprint takes a different route, using a Gumbel-Softmax straight-through surrogate to bring GPU-scale gradient optimization to exact Gillespie-type CTMC simulation. What is new is that the domain-specific dynamics or constraints are retained as the scaffold, with learning applied to the components that are expensive, discrete, or otherwise difficult to differentiate.
